name: Béarn

limits: For red wine, Tannat: at least 50%
For rosé wine, Tannat: at least 20%
For white wine, Camaralet de Lasseube, Courbu, Lauzet, Petit Courbu and Sauvignon Blanc together: at most 30%

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.

blurb.text: A South West France appellation in three separate sectors: around Salies-de-Béarn and Bellocq in the west, south and west of Pau, and in a loop of the Adour to the northeast. Its rules allow Tannat, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon, along with Petit Manseng, Gros Manseng and Raffiat de Moncade.
